limitations: The information cutoff is 18 Nov 16:20 BRT and the US and Brazilian equity closes refer to 17 Nov.
The European Commission 2026–2028 forecasts and Nvidia's next-quarter guidance are projections, while October Eurostat/ONS figures are observed outcomes.
Anthropic's $900.9 billion figure comprises multi-year contractual commitments with different forms and maturities. It is not a single-year cash outlay or market capitalization.
Market index moves do not identify capital flows or private spreads without dedicated issuance and lending data.
Brazilian fiscal vote and October FOMC minutes are prospective at the information cutoff.

en.title: Global Macro — European energy inflation persists as AI capital commitments expand
en.deck: Eurostat confirms 4.0% euro-area inflation in October. Anthropic's filing details long-term AI computing commitments, while US data signal cost and demand tension.
en.regime: Persistent European energy inflation and rising AI infrastructure commitments amid mixed US demand and financing signals.
en.key_risk: Energy costs and multi-year investment liabilities may outlast the corresponding revenue and financing capacity.

revision_reason: Revised after independent QA rejection for insufficient depth in both locales. Adds the full 18 November Eurostat HICP release, ONS UK inflation, RBA minutes, Nvidia fiscal results, Anthropic's SEC filing, Brazilian fiscal agenda and official US retail/import-price/industrial-production releases.
qa_fixes_applied: Expanded both staged editions beyond the 1700 substantive-word minimum with source-supported original analysis.
Retained and checked bilingual parity of all chart numeric series and updated the analysis to the 18 November information cutoff.
Replaced outdated forward-looking Eurostat phrasing with final October HICP and revised energy component; kept FOMC minutes and Brazilian fiscal vote as pending at cutoff.
Added quantitative stock-versus-flow and multi-year contractual-commitment analysis for the AI infrastructure cycle.
contrary_evidence: Eurostat's final energy rate rose relative to the flash estimate while the overall 4.0% rate was unchanged.
US manufacturing output rose 0.3% despite a 0.4% fall in aggregate industrial production.
The RBA recorded a divided six-to-three decision, evidencing uncertainty about optimal restrictive policy.
UK unemployment declined in a rolling-quarter survey while provisional payroll employment weakened.
US sovereign yields eased while multiple equity indexes fell.
